question: Should OpenClaw commit to a public Plugin SDK readiness-registration API and four built-in hosting profiles as supported compatibility contracts before this stacked implementation proceeds?
rationale: This is a durable API and operator-facing configuration direction, not a mechanical defect that review automation can safely choose on maintainers’ behalf.

options.title: Approve the staged readiness direction
options.body: Accept the public readiness registration contract and built-in profiles, then require the prerequisites to land and this branch to be rebased with integrated proof.

options.title: Keep readiness core-only for V1
options.body: Land or pursue only core-owned readiness observations and defer plugin registration plus hosting profiles until a narrower owner-approved design exists.

options.title: Pause the RFC 0023 stack
options.body: Close or defer the profile branches until maintainers sponsor a deployment-readiness product contract and its upgrade policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the staged readiness direction
recommendation.body: Accept the public readiness registration contract and built-in profiles, then require the prerequisites to land and this branch to be rebased with integrated proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The author owns the declared stacked implementation and can clarify or narrow the proposed API and profile boundaries for maintainer review.
